title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes, Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, combinatorial foundation for tame or stratified topology, in the spirit of the 'topologie modérée' of Esquisse d'un programme. The ingredients are:
- L, a set of 'lieux' (points);
- \mathcal M, a set of 'multistrates' (stratified pieces);
- for X in \mathcal M, the support L_X ⊂ L and the open strata L_X^° of X;
- a partial order ≤ (closed sub-multistrate);
- a relation ≪ (refinement or containment of stratifications);
- a relation R (compatibility).

The previous page (p.23) proved that inside a figure F the open strata L_X^° partition the support. It also proved that X ↦ L_X is injective and that X ≤ Y ⇔ L_X ⊂ L_Y ⇔ L_X^° ∩ L_Y ≠ ∅.

This page states the 'reciprocal' results. To each multistrate X one attaches \hat L_X ⊂ \mathcal P(L), the set of its open strata, viewed as subsets of L.
(a) X ≪ Y iff every open stratum of X is contained in some open stratum of Y. In modern terms, ≪ is a refinement relation read off the families of strata.
(b) X and Y are compatible iff any open stratum of X and any open stratum of Y are either disjoint or identical.

Corollaries:
(a) \hat L_X = \hat L_Y ⇔ X = Y.
(b) \hat L_X ⊂ \hat L_Y with \hat L_X 'closed' in \hat L_Y (stable under passing to strata in the closure, i.e. a down-set for the frontier/specialization order) ⇔ X ≤ Y.

Scholie: the whole structure (\mathcal M, ≤, ≪, R) can be recovered purely from L and the family \hat{\mathcal M} = Im(X ↦ \hat L_X). This is an injective map \mathcal M → \mathcal P(\mathcal P(L)), so \hat{\mathcal M} ∈ \mathcal P(\mathcal P(\mathcal P(L))).

The point of the page is to show that multistrates are redundant data: a stratified object can be identified with its set of strata. This is exactly what motivates the restart on p.25 ('On reprend tout!'). There a 'contrée' is defined as a set L of lieux plus a family \mathcal F ⊂ \mathcal P(\mathcal P(L)) of 'figures', each figure being a set of strata, and axioms (Cont 1, …) are to be extracted.

The diagonal marginal note ('Attention! … réciproques … contre-exemple … mais …') indicates Grothendieck noticed that some of these converses fail, or need extra hypotheses, in the current axiomatics. This is a further reason for recasting everything with figures-as-sets-of-strata as the primitive notion.
errors: The reciprocal statements (a) and (b) are asserted without proof. The marginal note explicitly flags a possible counterexample to the converses, so in the p.21–23 axiomatics they are likely not provable as stated. Grothendieck's own response is to restart with them built into the definition (p.25).

In (b), 'compatible' is characterized as 'strata pairwise disjoint or identical'. This is stronger than the usual notion of compatible stratifications (existence of a common refinement). It only matches if compatibility means that X ∪ Y is again a multistrate.
In Cor (b), 'closed in \hat L_Y' is undefined on this page. It presumably means stability under the frontier/specialization relation between strata.

ideas.what: Identify a stratified object with the set of its (open) strata, a subset of P(L), and recover order, refinement and compatibility relations from set-theoretic relations among strata
ideas.modern_name: stratification as a partition into strata / poset of strata; definable cell decompositions in o-minimal geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney–Thom–Mather (stratifications); van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (o-minimal tame topology, 1980s–1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (tame topology, informal program only); the 1986 axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: Refinement criterion: X ≪ Y iff each open stratum of X lies in an open stratum of Y; compatibility iff strata are disjoint or equal
A geometric universe ('contrée') encoded as an element of P(P(P(L))): points, figures = sets of strata, axioms to be extracted
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame geometry / structure in the sense of o-minimality (a family of definable sets), but with stratified figures as primitives

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'contrée' axiomatics for tame topology takes stratified figures (sets of strata) as primitive objects instead of definable sets. This differs from the o-minimal approach, and this transitional page shows why: multistrates are recoverable from their strata. As far as I know this framework has not been developed or compared with o-minimal structures or with stratified-space/exit-path formalisms.
missed.quote: On récupère M, avec ≪, R (compatibilité) en termes de L, et de l'ens. des \hat L_X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Specialists in tame geometry and in combinatorial models of stratified spaces (exit-path categories, poset-stratified spaces) might find a strata-first axiomatics worth comparing with o-minimality. The idea itself is elementary, however.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a transitional bookkeeping step: stratified objects are determined by their sets of strata. It is mathematically routine, though historically interesting because it motivates the 'contrée' definition on the next page, in Grothendieck's little-studied 1986 tame-topology axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: Item (a) reads: 'il faut et il suffit que toute strate ouverte de X soit contenue dans une strate ouverte de Y'.
Item (b) ends roughly: '…pour toute strate ouverte de X et toute strate ouverte de Y, celles-ci soient disjointes ou identiques'.
Line 4 is roughly 'Ils permettent, grâce aux relations de réciproques, de [récupérer] les strates …' (uncertain); 'structures maximales' is likely 'strates'.
Left marginal note begins 'Attention! en vue des réciproques … contre-exemples … mais …'.
'Contrats' in the margin is possibly 'Contrées' or 'Contrats', uncertain.
The second marginal note lists f_X, f'_X, δf_X, δf'_X (uncertain).
